goal: Produce a grounded, evidence-cited design proposal for whether/how to bring pmcro-runtime's MAF declarative workflow, Harness, and CodeAct patterns into pmcr-o's own governed PMCR-O cycle, without implementing any of it yet.

steps.action: Re-check pmcro-runtime current state (git status/log on both diverging local copies, content search for Harness/CodeAct/CopilotKit) to ground the proposal in fresh evidence rather than the prior session summary alone.
Read pmcr-o current state (STATE.md, AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md, plugins/ layout) to ground the "what stays" section accurately.

Write .pmcro/design/maf-declarative-migration-proposal.md: current state, what pmcro-runtime has proven vs not proven (with specific evidence), three graduated options (A: CodeAct pilot, B: Harness-style skill provider, C: full declarative migration), invariants that must not change, risk register, recommendation, open decisions for the user.

Verify the document does not overstate pmcro-runtime maturity -- confirm every claim of "proven" cites specific evidence (a file, a commit tag, a comment) and every open gap from migration-status.md and the Find() bug is represented, not glossed over.
Commit and push the new design document. No other files touched -- this cycle makes no code changes.

success_criteria: Document accurately reflects pmcr-o's current PowerShell-script-based PMCR-O mechanism and governance invariants, not a hypothetical
Document distinguishes what pmcro-runtime has actually proven (with citations) from what it has not, including the documented Find() SDK bug and open migration-status.md gates
Document proposes graduated options (not a single all-or-nothing recommendation) with an explicit risk register
Document explicitly states it is a proposal only -- no code or runtime behavior changes in this cycle
Document committed and pushed to origin
out_of_scope: Implementing any of options A/B/C -- explicitly deferred pending user decision
Modifying pmcro-runtime itself -- user scoped that repo to review/report only
Filing a next_seed for implementation work -- which option to pursue is the user's decision, not this cycle's to presume
name_rationale: Names exactly what this cycle produces: a migration design proposal, not an implementation.
